_note: # Defender Lesson 2: Defending the HVAC System

Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) controllers look harmless, but they're a favorite foothold for attackers: they sit on building networks, they're rarely patched, and they speak ModBus - a protocol with no built-in authentication at all. In this lesson you monitor a live HVAC controller through the AP you secured in lesson 1, learning what "normal" looks like so you can spot when something isn't.

The Polled Packets (Last 10) panel shows the latest readings the AP reports, and the Defender Monitors strip charts plot them over time. You'll watch temperature setpoints, fan states, and heating/cooling modes change, then compare what you see before and after turning encryption and the AP tunnel on and off. The key habit this lesson builds is baselining: a defender who knows the normal rhythm of a system notices the first odd beat.

- Connect to the AP and confirm the HVAC model is being driven by live telemetry.
- Identify each HVAC reading in the Polled Packets panel and what physical value it represents.
- Use the strip charts to describe the system's normal operating pattern.
- Explain why ModBus traffic is dangerous to leave unencrypted on a shared network.
- Use the Packet Log and Defender Flags to notice a value that falls outside its normal range.
